item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.8.1
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 8.1

Ask says when something isn't in your meetings. When you ask about a person, a project or a thing that your meetings never mention, Ask now says it couldn't find it and shows the closest match, instead of answering from a line that sounds similar. Answers also arrive faster.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.8
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 8

Notes that read like a document. Each note opens with what the meeting settled in two or three sentences, then a section for each topic under its own heading, with the decision first and its reasons under it. Points that only repeat a decision are gone, names are credited only where the transcript backs them, and steps start with the action. The page is set for reading, with clearer headings and stronger contrast.

More decisions caught. A separate pass looks for what the meeting settled, including a proposal agreed with a short "yes" and a choice reached over several turns. Long meetings keep their decisions and steps. Names the meeting already knows, from the invite, your people, your projects and your dictionary, are spelled right in the transcript.

Ask Tailwing, from anywhere. Ask is in the sidebar and on ⌘J, and asks about the page you're on: a meeting, a person, an organization, a project or all your notes. Make writes a follow-up email, a brief for the next meeting or a summary for your manager in one step. Ask now reads each meeting's decisions, next steps, people and dates, and searches by meaning in English meetings, so questions across meetings get answered. Your question stays in the field until an answer is on its way, and if Ask can't answer, it says why.

A catalog of your meetings, built on this Mac. While your Mac is idle or plugged in, Tailwing files a card for each meeting and keeps a running summary for each person, organization and project. Ask reads them first. Private meetings are never included. You can pause it in Settings, Models.

Live transcript in the note. While notes are running, the note shows the transcript as it arrives. After Stop it says "Writing notes…" and the sections arrive one by one. Write Up Again shows its progress straight away and keeps the old note readable until the new one lands. Rewrite Older Notes offers to bring earlier notes up to this version, in the background, keeping every earlier version and skipping notes you edited.

Before and after a meeting. The meeting banner offers Remind Me in 5 Minutes, and asks which call to follow when two overlap. The brief for your next meeting arrives on its own. After a meeting, Tailwing can draft a follow-up email in your mail app, written on this Mac, to the people who attended. Pro features can be tried free a few times, at the moment they help.

Calendar. This Week is now Calendar, with day and week views over the hours your meetings take. Meetings with notes open them, and an upcoming meeting shows its brief.

Spoken translation in German and Ukrainian. Translation is spoken between English and German and between English and Ukrainian, a clause at a time. If a better voice for a language can be downloaded, Tailwing says where.

Screen-share captures (Pro). When turned on in Settings, Meetings, Tailwing keeps a picture of the shared screen in Zoom or Google Meet each time it changes, with its text, inline in the transcript. Pictures stay on this Mac. Their text is used like the transcript.

Camera with Tailwing. An optional camera that shows a small "Taking notes with Tailwing" label on your video. Set it up in Settings, Meetings.

Video notes start on their own. When a video is playing and no call is on, Tailwing takes notes from the Mac's sound only, with the microphone off. A video's notes have no next steps or decisions; its instructions appear as steps shown.

Next Steps in bulk. Select several steps to move, finish or clear them together, including on a project page. Ticking a step in a note moves it to Done with Undo. Every row that can belong to a project uses the same control.

Faster. Opening a meeting is several times faster, Today and People switch in about half the time, and long notes scroll more smoothly.

Fixes.

  • Actions across the app say when they worked and, when they didn't, why and what to do: saves, sends, copies, moves, downloads and removals.
  • A note's day on a next step shows in every language.
  • In your own notes and lists, you are "you".
  • The Neural Engine is used for speech whenever your Mac has one and one of your languages is supported.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.7
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 7

Video mode. Tailwing can take notes on a video by capturing only the Mac's sound. Your microphone is never opened, and there is no coaching or cue. Switch a take to or from video from the pill's menu. On first run, Try it on a video writes your first note from any video you play.

Dictation keeps your first words. The microphone is ready before you press, so the start of a sentence is no longer lost, and the text lands at the keystroke without a pause.

A call that goes wrong still leaves notes. If Tailwing closes unexpectedly or the power fails, the meeting is recovered from its audio, with a line saying where notes stopped. If the Mac sleeps mid-call, Tailwing offers the meeting back on wake and says it paused. When space runs low, the pill says how many minutes of notes still fit. If a second call starts while notes are running, Tailwing asks before switching and captures nothing from the new call until you press. When a long meeting's write-up leaves out a stretch, the note says which one, and Try Again writes up just that part.

Speaker names need evidence. A name is written only when the meeting supports it, such as someone saying their own name or being called by it. Otherwise Tailwing suggests, and you choose. Each name says why it was given, and the people invited are offered first. Names are never matched by voice.

Live translation covers many more languages. Subtitles are offered between the 13 languages Apple's Translation installs, up to three lines at a time on a bar that stays readable over any video. A sentence is never silently skipped. One that arrives late is marked "Not translated yet" and filled in when it does, and the bar says when it is catching up. Spoken translation stays on the pairs measured to keep up. Live translation is still experimental.

People and organizations by when you last met. Filter either list by Last Met, from the last month to not met in six months. An organization's page shows its last contact and next meeting.

Calendar events from your Mac's Calendar. Events from Exchange and iCloud calendars now count in carry-over and the weekly recap. Copy and Export include only events the calendar still holds.

Today as one agenda. Times sit in a gutter, past notes show their day, and rows share one form. Decisions has one Filter menu with removable tokens. Plain Notes moved inside All Notes, and AI Tools has its own tab in Settings.

Ask cites by time. Each answer links the moments it draws on as times that open the transcript at that line, and speaks to you as "you".

Private by default. Onboarding now says nothing is uploaded unless you turn it on. The Neural Engine is on by default on any supported Mac when Accurate is chosen, for the languages it hears.

Better notes. Notes now open with what the meeting decided, and keep the principle that guided the calls. Decisions show the choice the meeting ended on, not one it moved past or only thought aloud about. Instructions appear as next steps, with the person who took them on. Things already done, or that happen only if something else does, stay out of your next steps. Attendee lists drop greetings and duplicate names, words from your dictionary are spelled the way you spell them, and in your own notes you appear as "you", while anything you share still uses your name.

Fixes.

  • Notes are ended with Stop everywhere, where some places said Finish.
  • Share opens under the Share button. Invites are one row: Share, Copy Message, Copy Link.
  • A decision or next step can be moved to another project again from the project page.
  • Subtitles stay readable over a white video.
  • When renaming a speaker leaves next steps without an owner, the note says so.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.6
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 6

One size of text. Rows, the sidebar, buttons and the toolbar now share one size, and only page titles are larger. Settings follows the same sizes. Pages sit on the plain background in one column, with sections separated by a thin rule, and selection is a neutral fill with heavier text.

A meeting's note is one document. The note scrolls as a single, wider page. The transcript's lines sit on one grid. Next Steps no longer scrolls through its header.

Names stay hidden wherever notes leave this Mac. Anonymize and Hide everyone's names now apply to every answer an AI tool gets through the connector, to the local API and Shortcuts, to the webhook and folder outputs, and to Share Notes, Copy and Save. If names can't be removed, nothing is handed over and Tailwing says why. Export Everything stays a complete copy unless Anonymize is on.

More for your AI tools. A connected tool can ask for the context of a meeting or a person in one call. With your own Clay account connected, that context includes the role, organization and profile link of a person you have looked up. None of it is sent while names are hidden. The people list, a person's page and a meeting's brief through the connector are part of Pro.

Across your meetings, with Pro. A recurring meeting has a page of its own: what changed since last time, what is still open, and each past meeting. Before a meeting, From last time lists what carried over. A weekly recap gathers the week's meetings, decisions, and open and overdue next steps; its headline is free every week. The first three uses of each are complete without Pro.

Photos and logos. Tailwing can show people's photos and company logos beside their names, from Contacts, Gravatar and each company's website. Nothing is looked up until you press Got It, and never for a private meeting or in Private mode. The choices are in Settings, Privacy.

Dictation on a mouse button. Hold a mouse button to dictate. Choose it in Settings, Shortcuts.

Live translation is experimental. It can fall behind when this Mac is busy, so Tailwing no longer offers it during a call. You can turn it on in Settings. Translation after the meeting is unaffected.

Fixes.

  • Share Notes and Send in Export sent names when only Hide everyone's names was on. They now hide them.
  • Your own second email address is no longer listed as an attendee.
  • Empty items such as "None" are no longer stored as decisions or next steps.
  • Decisions show people's names where they showed email addresses.
  • Placeholder text in every field is now easier to read in every look.
  • Tailwing could close unexpectedly after quitting while something was still reading your notes. It now closes cleanly.
  • A change made on one Mac no longer bounces back and forth between two Macs after a relaunch.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.5
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 5

One focused column. A meeting now opens as a single column with larger text, and the sidebar and toolbar step aside while you read. Press Escape to go back to Home. Settings, General, Show every place and button brings the full window back.

A simpler Home. Home is one page: your day first, then your notes grouped by date. Notes, People and Projects filter the list. The rest of the places are under More.

Flight is the look for everyone. New installs start in Flight, and anyone on Instrument is moved to it once. You can switch back in Settings, General, Look. Flight has a new manner: a calm, focused layout, with Decisions and Next Steps in one card that shows each step's owner and day, a time beside each line Tailwing wrote that opens the transcript at that moment so you can see where it came from, a day card on Home, and new icons and type.

Folio, a second look. Folio sets your notes on warm paper with serif titles and notes. It is free, and it is the second choice in Settings, General, Look.

Your day. Coming Up and This Week can show a day as well as a list, with a block for each meeting and a line that sums it up, such as how many meetings there are and when you next have an hour free. Next Steps now starts with Today and Upcoming. Quick Add, a small field for a to-do, is off until you choose a key in Settings, Shortcuts.

Share Notes. Share Notes in a meeting prepares a clean email of its notes, and Send Their Next Steps on a person's steps does the same for one person. You see exactly what will go and to whom, and you send it from your own mail app or copy it. Tailwing sends nothing itself. It is not offered for a private meeting.

Export Everything. Settings, Privacy, Your data, and the File menu, write your whole library to a new folder on this Mac. It never writes into or changes anything that was already in the place you choose.

AI tools that make changes. AI tools you have connected can suggest titles, speaker names, projects and folders, add their own notes and to-dos, flag moments, create a project, and ask Tailwing a question that comes back with links to the lines behind the answer. Each kind of change has its own switch in Settings, Connections, AI tools, and all of them are off until you turn on Let AI tools make changes. Suggestions wait under the meeting's title until you click Use, and Undo puts back what was there. For each tool you can also choose Apply without asking, which is off by default. A tool only changes or deletes items it added itself, and private meetings are never read or changed.

Faster, more trustworthy Ask. Answers appear as they are written, and each figure, quote and name is checked against the line it cites. Anything a line doesn't support is withdrawn.

Private meetings keep their owners. Notes for a private meeting are now written from what was said, before names are replaced, so next steps keep their owners and decisions keep their reasons. Only the replaced text is stored. A private meeting keeps no location.

A check on earlier private meetings. On a Mac that has had Pro, this release checks the private meetings you already have. Where an earlier version stored one without replacing names, Tailwing replaces them now and tells you how many meetings it changed.

Private meetings and sync. A private meeting's notes and audio stay on the Mac they were made on, and copies that earlier versions sent to iCloud are removed. If you sync between Macs, update all of them to this release: a Mac still on Beta 4 deletes its own copy of a private meeting's notes when another Mac removes them from iCloud.

Look up a person. On a person's page, Look Up fetches their title and organization from your own Apollo or Clay account. It appears only after you connect one in Settings, Connections, and it is part of Pro. Apollo is sent a name, an email address and the company's web domain, and Clay is sent a name and the company's web domain. Lookups use your own account and its credits.

Gift codes. Invite people from Settings, Invites, and you can earn up to three gift codes. Each code gives Pro on one Mac. To move a code to a new Mac, turn Pro off on the old one and enter the code on the new one in Settings, Pro, under Have a gift code?.

Live translation, where it keeps up. Live translation is offered only where it has been measured to keep up: the first words show within four seconds of a sentence starting, and the whole sentence about two seconds after it ends. Today that is English speech into Spanish, French, German, Italian and Portuguese. Every other language gets Translation after the meeting, with your notes written in your language. Spoken translation stops when you start talking.

  • A weekly count: once a week, one update check also carries a code that is different every week, so tailwing.co can count how many Macs use Tailwing. The code doesn't identify your Mac. It is on, and you can switch it off in Settings, Privacy, What leaves this Mac, Weekly count.

Settings and screen shares. When you share your screen, Tailwing hides Settings only on the panes that show people or text, so you can share the others.

Quitting. Command-Q asks whether to keep Tailwing in the menu bar so it can take notes for your next meeting. While a meeting is in progress it asks before it stops taking notes. You can set the answer once in Settings, General.

Fixes.

  • Dictation no longer quits the app when the microphone setup changes as it starts, such as when a dock or display is connected.
  • An AI tool sending an absurd number can no longer crash the app.
  • Side-panel text is no longer cut off at narrow widths.
  • The site and the app said Tailwing keeps each meeting's audio. Audio is deleted once the transcript and write-up are made, unless you choose to keep it in Settings, Privacy.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.8.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 8.2

Notes now stop by themselves when a browser call ends. After a Meet in Chrome, Tailwing could go on taking notes until you stopped it: Chrome kept hold of the microphone, and a normal room is rarely quiet enough for Tailwing to decide the call was over.

This version watches the same signal as the orange microphone dot in your menu bar, so leaving the call ends notes within seconds. If you were only stepping away, the call taking the microphone again within two minutes picks up the same meeting.

The AI tools connector is still paused, as in RC 8.1. It comes back in the next release.
